title: Control-Bridge paired-sample canary for pinned model revisions
creator: Elena Kim
description:
Objective: Safely validate new model revisions that will be exposed via 'pins' by running a paired-sample canary (Control-Bridge) and lightweight A/B evaluations without exposing users to degraded quality or unexpected latency tail behavior.

Background: Pinned model updates require conservative rollout because apps rely on deterministic behavior and cost/latency budgets. Existing canary patterns either mirror traffic (no user-facing split) or split live traffic into cohorts. Mirror-only approaches miss the paired-output comparisons useful for fine-grained quality regressions; naive cohort splits introduce customer-visible variance.

Proposal summary: Implement a Control-Bridge canary mode that: (1) routes a small percentage of live requests to the pinned revision as a mirrored secondary call, (2) captures paired outputs (control=model currently pinned, candidate=new revision) and stores differential metrics and artifacts in a blinded evaluation store, (3) runs paired-sample statistical tests on quality signals and token-level divergence metrics, and (4) gates progressive exposure with combined quality and latency-tail thresholds. The Control-Bridge supports an optional light A/B slice where certain non-sensitive cohorts are exposed to the candidate to measure behavior under real user conditions while maintaining a fast rollback path.

Key innovations vs. prior work: Introduces a "paired-sample" evaluation pipeline that directly compares outputs for identical inputs (prefix and context), plus a Control-Bridge policy that couples mirrored paired-eval with controlled cohort exposure for signal richness. Adds latency-tail gating (p99.9 and p99.99) to avoid tail regressions, and differential instrumentation for token-level divergences to isolate hallucination regressions.

Gating signals and thresholds (initial):
- Quality: paired BLEU-like / ROUGE-like similarity bucket + model-specific semantic similarity (embedding cosine) with alert if mean similarity drops > 4% and > 95th percentile regression magnitude.
- Safety: any safety classifier regression where false-positive reduction < -2% triggers immediate hold.
- Latency: p99.9 increase > 20% OR p99.99 increase > 10% triggers rollback.
- Error rate: 5xx increase > 1.5x baseline triggers rollback.

Rollout phases:
1) Dry-run mirrored paired-eval (0% user exposure). Collect 100k paired requests across relevant routes.
2) Blinded statistical validation and internal review (sigs: Platform, Research, Reliability).
3) Controlled cohort exposure (0.1% -> 1% -> 5%), each step only after passing gating checks for 48h.
4) Full promotion to pinned revision if no regressions for 7 days and stakeholder signoff.

Data privacy: Paired outputs stored in the evaluation store will be pseudonymized. Any customer PII will be redacted; team must coordinate with Security for retention policy and KMS usage.

Open questions:
- Which similarity metrics are best for open-ended generation categories (long-form completion vs. structured)? (Research to propose.)
- How to prioritize which routes are eligible for cohort exposure (cost vs. signal trade-offs)?
- SLO definitions for custom customer pins vs. platform defaults.

Stakeholders: Product (Elena Kim), Platform/Runtime (Marco Jensen), Research (Dr. Aisha Patel), Reliability (Daniel Ortiz), Security (Maya Singh).
acceptance_criteria: Control-Bridge mode implemented in routing layer to mirror requests and capture paired outputs
Paired-eval store receives and indexes paired outputs with request metadata and instrumentation tags
Automated paired-sample comparison pipeline computes configured similarity and divergence metrics within 24 hours
Gating engine can evaluate combined signals (quality + latency + safety) and produce a deterministic pass/fail for each rollout step
Runbook and rollback playbook documented and tested in a tabletop exercise
Security review completed and data retention policy for paired outputs approved
implementation_notes: Routing: add a new header 'X-Redwood-Control-Bridge' to mirrored calls and ensure KV-cache bypass behavior is consistent for mirrored requests
Instrumentation: capture token sampling (first/last 256 tokens) and per-token logprobs for divergence metrics; store embeddings for semantic similarity
Storage: evaluation store will be S3-backed with per-tenant prefixes and KMS encryption; index minimal metadata into BigQuery for analytics
Stat tests: start with paired cosine(embeddings) + token-level KL divergence; collaborate with Research on thresholds
Cohorts: default to non-sensitive, high-signal internal cohorts; product to define route allowlist
Dashboards: provide per-route paired-diff and latency tail charts in Console; flag regressions per release rollup
